wilsons-promontory-1.name: Mount Oberon
wilsons-promontory-1.bio: Granite summit walk from Telegraph Saddle with views of the coast, Tidal River and offshore islands; 6.8 km return.

wilsons-promontory-2.name: Squeaky Beach
wilsons-promontory-2.bio: Quartz sand that squeaks underfoot, between granite boulders near Tidal River; unpatrolled, with strong currents.

wilsons-promontory-3.name: Norman Beach
wilsons-promontory-3.bio: Sheltered swimming and snorkelling beach beside the Tidal River camp and estuary in Wilsons Promontory.

wilsons-promontory-4.name: Wilsons Promontory Lightstation
wilsons-promontory-4.bio: Granite lighthouse lit in 1859 at South East Point, the southernmost on mainland Australia, reached only on foot.

wilsons-promontory-5.name: Whisky Bay
wilsons-promontory-5.bio: Sunset beach with granite headlands at either end, a 700 m walk from Tidal River in Wilsons Promontory.

wilsons-promontory-6.name: Mount Bishop
wilsons-promontory-6.bio: A 7.4 km return walk from Lilly Pilly Gully through rainforest to a summit with views over the west coast and islands.

wilsons-promontory-7.name: Tongue Point
wilsons-promontory-7.bio: A 3.8 km one-way walk from Darby River over an ancient sand dune to granite tors and a boulder-covered island.

wilsons-promontory-8.name: Lilly Pilly Gully
wilsons-promontory-8.bio: A flat 5.2 km gravel nature walk through shaded rainforest, where wallabies and Superb Fairy-wrens are common.

croajingolong-1.name: Mallacoota
croajingolong-1.bio: Inlet town beside Top and Bottom lakes, the last township on Victoria's east coast before the NSW border.

croajingolong-2.name: Point Hicks Lightstation
croajingolong-2.bio: Granite headland where Captain Cook first sighted mainland Australia, with a historic lighthouse in Croajingolong National Park.

croajingolong-3.name: Gabo Island Lightstation
croajingolong-3.bio: 47 m pink-granite lighthouse off Mallacoota, Victoria's only operating island lighthouse, reached by boat or aircraft.

croajingolong-4.name: Wilderness Coast Walk
croajingolong-4.bio: Multi-day walk from Bemm River to Mallacoota along isolated coast and estuaries; navigation by map and compass.

croajingolong-5.name: Thurra River Sand Dunes
croajingolong-5.bio: Dunes 30 m high, the biggest in Victoria, a short walk from Thurra River Campground near Point Hicks.

croajingolong-6.name: Bastion Point
croajingolong-6.bio: Surf beach and headland lookout near Mallacoota, with views along the Croajingolong coast.

croajingolong-7.name: Genoa Peak
croajingolong-7.bio: Steep climb in Croajingolong to a summit with wide views over East Gippsland's inlets, forests and coast.

croajingolong-8.name: Fly Cove Walk
croajingolong-8.bio: Walk from Wingan Inlet Campground to sandy beaches and Fly Cove, where fur seals bask on rocky islets.

gippsland-lakes-1.name: Lakes Entrance
gippsland-lakes-1.bio: Town beside the channel linking the Gippsland Lakes to Bass Strait, with cruises, fishing charters and beaches.

gippsland-lakes-2.name: Ninety Mile Beach
gippsland-lakes-2.bio: A continuous surf beach of about 90 miles along Gippsland's coast, reached from Lakes Entrance.

gippsland-lakes-3.name: Metung
gippsland-lakes-3.bio: Village on a peninsula between Lake King and Bancroft Bay, with a marina boardwalk beside Legend Rock.

gippsland-lakes-4.name: Griffiths Sea Shell Museum and Marine Display
gippsland-lakes-4.bio: Private collection of over 90,000 shells and sea creatures, with a 10 m coral reef and an aquarium of Bass Strait life.

gippsland-lakes-5.name: Bairnsdale
gippsland-lakes-5.bio: Commercial hub of East Gippsland, a city of about 17,700 people on the way to the Gippsland Lakes.

south-gippsland-1.name: Inverloch
south-gippsland-1.bio: Surf beach town in South Gippsland with a foreshore walking track and the Bunurong coast's rock platforms close by.

south-gippsland-2.name: Cape Liptrap Coastal Park
south-gippsland-2.bio: Coastal park with lime kiln ruins, a working lighthouse and walks between Venus Bay and Waratah Bay.

south-gippsland-3.name: Bunurong Marine National Park
south-gippsland-3.bio: Marine park of sandstone rock platforms near Inverloch, best explored within an hour or so of low tide.

south-gippsland-4.name: Agnes Falls
south-gippsland-4.bio: The Agnes River drops 59 m into a gorge, reached by a 200 m walk and best after heavy rain.

south-gippsland-5.name: Wonthaggi State Coal Mine
south-gippsland-5.bio: Former state coal mine, worked 1910 to 1968, with free aboveground displays, a visitor film and a heritage trail.

south-gippsland-6.name: Coal Creek Community Park and Museum
south-gippsland-6.bio: Recreated coal-mining village of around 50 buildings from the 1870s to 1920s at Korumburra, with free entry.

south-gippsland-7.name: Great Southern Rail Trail
south-gippsland-7.bio: About 130 km rail trail linking 14 towns from Nyora to Alberton through dairy country, for walkers and cyclists.

south-gippsland-8.name: Leongatha
south-gippsland-8.bio: Main service town of South Gippsland, in the Strzelecki Ranges foothills 135 km south-east of Melbourne.

sale.name: Sale
sale.bio: Gippsland city of about 19,000 people and seat of Wellington Shire, home to the Gippsland Art Gallery.

sale-swing-bridge.name: Sale Swing Bridge
sale-swing-bridge.bio: An 1883 wrought-iron swing bridge on the Latrobe River 5 km south of Sale, with its hand-cranking system retained.

gippsland-art-gallery.name: Gippsland Art Gallery
gippsland-art-gallery.bio: Regional gallery in Sale with permanent Annemieke Mein textile art and a Borun & Tuk gallery of local First Nations art.

old-gippstown.name: Old Gippstown
old-gippstown.bio: Open-air museum of a reconstructed pioneer township on Lloyd Street in Moe, open Wednesday to Sunday.

walhalla.name: Walhalla
walhalla.bio: Former gold-mining town of about 20 residents, with underground mine tours, a goldfields railway and a cemetery.

baw-baw-national-park.name: Baw Baw National Park
baw-baw-national-park.bio: National park on the Baw Baw Plateau with snowgum forest, granite tors at Mushroom Rocks and snow play in winter.

mount-baw-baw.name: Mount Baw Baw
mount-baw-baw.bio: Alpine resort village at 1450 m in snow gum forest, Melbourne's closest ski resort, with summer walks and biking.

toorongo-falls.name: Toorongo Falls
toorongo-falls.bio: A 25 m waterfall with a viewing platform, reached by a forest walk near Noojee that continues to Amphitheatre Falls.

tarra-bulga-national-park.name: Tarra-Bulga National Park
tarra-bulga-national-park.bio: Cool-temperate rainforest park in South Gippsland with fern-lined creek walks and Corrigan's Suspension Bridge.

corrigans-suspension-bridge.name: Corrigan's Suspension Bridge
corrigans-suspension-bridge.bio: Suspension bridge through the rainforest canopy in Tarra-Bulga National Park, with views down into the fern gully.

port-albert.name: Port Albert
port-albert.bio: Corner Inlet town and one of Victoria's earliest ports, settled in 1841, with a maritime museum on Tarraville Road.

snowy-river-national-park.name: Snowy River National Park
snowy-river-national-park.bio: Remote East Gippsland park where the Snowy River cuts through Tulloch Ard Gorge, with gorge walks and canoe access.

buchan-caves.name: Buchan Caves
buchan-caves.bio: Victoria's largest cave system, seen only on guided tours of Royal Cave or Fairy Cave, near Buchan in East Gippsland.

errinundra-national-park.name: Errinundra National Park
errinundra-national-park.bio: Plateau park of cool-temperate rainforest, with a rainforest boardwalk, Ocean View Lookout and camping.

cape-conran-coastal-park.name: Cape Conran Coastal Park
cape-conran-coastal-park.bio: Far-east coastal park near Marlo with wild ocean beaches, Yeerung Gorge rock pools and whale-watching May to October.

den-of-nargun.name: Den of Nargun
den-of-nargun.bio: Loop walk in Mitchell River National Park to a waterfall cave said to house the Nargun; please stay out of the cave.

mitchell-river-national-park-vic.name: Mitchell River National Park
mitchell-river-national-park-vic.bio: Gippsland gorge park with a walk to the Den of Nargun, Billy Goat Bend lookout and Grade III-IV whitewater.
